review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: Δικαιωθέντες οὖν ἐκ πίστεως εἰρήνην ἔχωμεν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
5:1.targetText: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

groups.note: ἐκ ("from, by") is rendered through.
Same verb; BSB's Greek has another form of it here, rendered we have (N1904's subjunctive means "let us have").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle Δικαιωθέντες ("having been justified").

5:2.sourceText: δι’ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν ταύτην ἐν ᾗ ἑστήκαμεν, καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ.
5:2.targetText: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.

groups.note: The dative πίστει is rendered by faith.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:3.sourceText: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν, εἰδότες ὅτι ἡ θλῖψις ὑπομονὴν κατεργάζεται,
5:3.targetText: Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;

groups.note: The article ταῖς is rendered as the possessive our.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a demonstrative after Not only.
English supplies a subject for the participle εἰδότες ("knowing").

5:4.sourceText: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ δοκιμήν, ἡ δὲ δοκιμὴ ἐλπίδα·

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the first connective δέ untranslated.

5:5.sourceText: ἡ δὲ ἐλπὶς οὐ καταισχύνει, ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν διὰ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου τοῦ δοθέντος ἡμῖν.
5:5.targetText: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.

groups.note: καταισχύνει ("puts to shame") is rendered disappoint.
BSB makes God the subject; the article ἡ ("the" love) is rendered His.
The passive ἐκκέχυται ("has been poured out") is rendered has poured out, with God as subject.
The article with the passive participle δοθέντος ("given") is rendered whom … has given.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of disappoint.
English supplies God as the subject of the passive participle δοθέντος ("given").

5:6.sourceText: ἔτι γὰρ Χριστὸς ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν ἔτι κατὰ καιρὸν ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν ἀπέθανεν.
5:6.targetText: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ὄντων ἡμῶν ("we being") is rendered while we were.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the repeated ἔτι ("still") only once.

5:7.sourceText: μόλις γὰρ ὑπὲρ δικαίου τις ἀποθανεῖται· ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ τάχα τις καὶ τολμᾷ ἀποθανεῖν·
5:7.targetText: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.

groups.note: μόλις ("scarcely") is rendered Very rarely.
The adjective δικαίου ("a righteous one") is rendered a righteous man.
γάρ ("for") is rendered though.
τάχα ("perhaps") is rendered might possibly.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("even") untranslated here.

5:8.sourceText: συνίστησιν δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀγάπην εἰς ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ὅτι ἔτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὄντων ἡμῶν Χριστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν.
5:8.targetText: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

groups.note: ὅτι ("in that") is rendered in this, introducing the explanation.
The genitive absolute ὄντων ἡμῶν ("we being") is rendered While we were.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:9.sourceText: πολλῷ οὖν μᾶλλον δικαιωθέντες νῦν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ σωθησόμεθα δι’ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς.
5:9.targetText: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!

groups.note: ἐν ("in, by") is rendered by.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle δικαιωθέντες ("having been justified").

5:10.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὶ ὄντες κατηλλάγημεν τῷ Θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, πολλῷ μᾶλλον καταλλαγέντες σωθησόμεθα ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ·
5:10.targetText: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!

groups.note: BSB names God earlier, with enemies, and renders τῷ Θεῷ ("to God") as to Him.
ἐν ("in, by") is rendered through.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ὄντες ("being").
English names whose enemies; the Greek names God only after reconciled.

5:11.sourceText: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν τῷ Θεῷ διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ οὗ νῦν τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐλάβομεν.
5:11.targetText: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a demonstrative after Not only.
English supplies a subject for the participle καυχώμενοι ("rejoicing").

5:12.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο ὥσπερ δι’ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἡ ἁμαρτία εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθεν, καὶ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος, καὶ οὕτως εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁ θάνατος διῆλθεν, ἐφ’ ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον·
5:12.targetText: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.

groups.note: Διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered Therefore.
εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ("came into") is rendered by the transitive verb entered.
καὶ οὕτως ("and so") is rendered so also.
The active διῆλθεν ("spread, passed through") is rendered was passed on.
ἐφ’ ᾧ ("on the ground that") is rendered because.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:13.sourceText: ἄχρι γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία ἦν ἐν κόσμῳ, ἁμαρτία δὲ οὐκ ἐλλογεῖται μὴ ὄντος νόμου·
5:13.targetText: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.

groups.note: ἄχρι ("until") is rendered before.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek says only "until law".

5:14.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἐβασίλευσεν ὁ θάνατος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ μέχρι Μωϋσέως καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτήσαντας ἐπὶ τῷ ὁμοιώματι τῆς παραβάσεως Ἀδάμ, ὅς ἐστιν τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος.
5:14.targetText: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.

groups.note: ἀλλά ("but") is rendered Nevertheless.
The article with the participle ἁμαρτήσαντας ("having sinned") is rendered those who did … sin.
ὁμοιώματι ("likeness") is rendered way.
The noun παραβάσεως ("transgression") is rendered transgressed.
The relative ὅς ("who") begins a new English sentence as He.
The article with the participle μέλλοντος ("coming") is rendered of the One to come.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the clause made from the noun παραβάσεως ("transgression").

5:15.sourceText: Ἀλλ’ οὐχ ὡς τὸ παράπτωμα, οὕτως καὶ τὸ χάρισμα· εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι οἱ πολλοὶ ἀπέθανον, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι τῇ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἐπερίσσευσεν.
5:15.targetText: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!

groups.note: The genitive ἑνός ("of the one") is rendered of the one man.
The dative παραπτώματι is rendered by the trespass.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "not as the trespass, so also the gift" as one comparison, so οὕτως καί ("so also") has no English words.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative frame before by the grace.

5:16.sourceText: καὶ οὐχ ὡς δι’ ἑνὸς ἁμαρτήσαντος τὸ δώρημα· τὸ μὲν γὰρ κρίμα ἐξ ἑνὸς εἰς κατάκριμα, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα ἐκ πολλῶν παραπτωμάτων εἰς δικαίωμα.
5:16.targetText: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered Again.
δι’ ("through") is rendered the result of.
The participle ἁμαρτήσαντος ("who sinned") is rendered sin.
ἐξ ("from") is rendered that followed.
εἰς ("into, resulting in") is rendered brought.
ἐκ ("from") is rendered that followed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves μέν untranslated; the δέ that answers it is rendered but.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

5:17.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι ὁ θάνατος ἐβασίλευσεν διὰ τοῦ ἑνός, πολλῷ μᾶλλον οἱ τὴν περισσείαν τῆς χάριτος καὶ τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς δικαιοσύνης λαμβάνοντες ἐν ζωῇ βασιλεύσουσιν διὰ τοῦ ἑνὸς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
5:17.targetText: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!

groups.note: The dative παραπτώματι is rendered by the trespass.
The article τοῦ points back to the one man and is rendered that.
The article with the participle λαμβάνοντες ("receiving") is rendered those who receive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:18.sourceText: Ἄρα οὖν ὡς δι’ ἑνὸς παραπτώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς κατάκριμα, οὕτως καὶ δι’ ἑνὸς δικαιώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς δικαίωσιν ζωῆς·
5:18.targetText: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.

groups.note: εἰς ("into, resulting in") is rendered brought.
The genitive ζωῆς ("of life") is rendered and life.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes one trespass and one act of righteousness the subjects, so δι’ ("through") has no English word.

5:19.sourceText: ὥσπερ γὰρ διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοί, οὕτως καὶ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί.
5:19.targetText: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

groups.note: The genitive ἑνός ("of the one") is rendered of the one man.

5:20.sourceText: νόμος δὲ παρεισῆλθεν ἵνα πλεονάσῃ τὸ παράπτωμα· οὗ δὲ ἐπλεόνασεν ἡ ἁμαρτία, ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν ἡ χάρις,
5:20.targetText: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,

groups.note: The compound ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν ("overflowed beyond") is rendered increased all the more.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:21.sourceText: ἵνα ὥσπερ ἐβασίλευσεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ, οὕτως καὶ ἡ χάρις βασιλεύσῃ διὰ δικαιοσύνης εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν.
5:21.targetText: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

groups.note: εἰς ("unto") is rendered to bring.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
